sources.name: Moms on Call
sources.summary_one_line: Structured ~4-hour feeding routine with ~2-hour wake windows, 2-3 naps, 10-12h night sleep; solids after milk feeds.

sources.name: Taking Cara Babies
sources.summary_one_line: 5-6mo wake windows 2-3h; 3 naps typical, 3-4h day sleep, 10-12h night, ~14-15h total.

sources.name: Precious Little Sleep (Alexis Dubief)
sources.summary_one_line: Averages ~14-15h/24h at 5-6mo with 3 naps; emphasizes drowsy-but-awake and self-soothing.

sources.name: Ferber method
sources.summary_one_line: Graduated extinction with progressively longer check-ins; usually starts ~6 months.

sources.name: Weissbluth — Healthy Sleep Habits, Happy Child
sources.summary_one_line: Protect naps and early bedtime (6-8pm); ~14-15h/24h with 3 naps; avoid overtiredness.

sources.name: AAP / HealthyChildren.org
sources.summary_one_line: At 6mo: 6-8 oz x 4-5 feeds/day; ~11h night + naps to 14-15h; introduce solids.

sources.name: CDC — Infant Feeding & Milestones
sources.summary_one_line: Solids ~6mo when developmentally ready; milk remains main nutrition.

sources.name: WHO — Infant and Young Child Feeding
sources.summary_one_line: Exclusive BF to 6mo, then complementary foods 2-3x/day at 6-8mo.

sources.name: La Leche League International
sources.summary_one_line: Breastfed babies 1-6mo take ~3-5 oz per feed; feed on cue.

sources.name: KellyMom
sources.summary_one_line: Exclusively breastfed babies 1-6mo average ~25 oz/day (range 19-30 oz).

sources.name: Solid Starts
sources.summary_one_line: First foods ~6mo when ready; for reflux: delay solids 30+ min after milk, upright pacing.

sources.name: The Wonder Weeks — Leap 4
sources.summary_one_line: Leap 4 ('World of Events') ~19wk from due date; fussy 1-6wk; baby grasps cause/effect.

sources.name: Janet Lansbury / RIE
sources.summary_one_line: Respectful caregiving: observe before responding, narrate care, independent floor play.

sources.name: Mayo Clinic — Infant Acid Reflux
sources.summary_one_line: Feed upright, hold upright 30min after; smaller more frequent feeds; back-sleep even with reflux.

sources.name: NICHD Safe to Sleep
sources.summary_one_line: Always back-sleep, firm flat surface, no soft bedding; room-share without bed-sharing.

sources.name: CDC — Milestones by 6 Months
sources.summary_one_line: By 6mo: rolls both ways, pushes up, brings to mouth, recognizes faces, vocal turn-taking.

ounces_per_day_total.note: milk only, before solids dominate; BF ~25oz/day average (range 19-30); FF often 24-32oz/day

solids_intro_guidance.frequency_per_day: Start 1 meal/day for 1-2 weeks, build to 2-3 meals/day by 6-8mo; offer milk first.
solids_intro_guidance.amount_per_meal: 1-2 tsp to start; progress to 2-4 tbsp as tolerated; follow baby's cues.
solids_intro_guidance.reflux_considerations: Wait 20-30 min after milk feed; keep baby upright during and 20-30 min after eating; smaller more frequent milk feeds; avoid citrus/tomato/spicy early; thicker textures (oatmeal, banana) may stay down better; continue prescribed reflux meds.

reflux_tips: Hold baby upright for 20-30 minutes after every feed.
Smaller, more frequent feeds — avoid overfilling the stomach.
Paced bottle feeding (horizontal bottle, frequent breaks).
Burp during natural pauses mid-feed and at the end.
Always back-sleep on a firm flat surface; do not incline the crib (per NICHD/AAP).
Give nighttime reflux medication consistently as prescribed.
For solids: wait 20-30 min after milk; thicker textures often tolerated better.
Severe reflux: ask pediatrician about a 2-week dairy/soy elimination if breastfeeding.
Red flags for re-evaluation: poor weight gain, projectile vomiting, blood in spit-up, refusing feeds, persistent cough.
developmental_milestones_typical_at_5_5_: Pushes up on straight arms during tummy time.
Sits with support; some tripod-sit briefly.
Brings hands and objects to mouth; transfers between hands emerging.
Reaches for and grasps toys with raking grip.
Recognizes familiar faces; distinguishes caregivers from strangers.
Responds to own name; turns toward sounds.
Babbles with consonant sounds (ba, ma, da) and takes turns making sounds.
Shows interest in food — opens mouth, leans toward spoon (solids readiness).
Laughs, squeals, expresses range of emotions; stranger wariness emerging.
Wonder Weeks Leap 4 ('World of Events') — fussy/clingy phase possible around 5-5.5mo.
red_flags_to_watch: Fewer than 4-5 wet diapers in 24h, dark urine, dry mouth — possible dehydration.
Not gaining weight or crossing percentiles downward.
Forceful/projectile vomiting, blood or green/yellow bile in vomit.
Choking, gagging, turning blue, arching in pain with feeds.
Persistent cough, wheeze, recurrent respiratory infections.
No rolling in either direction by 6mo; very stiff or very floppy tone.
Not responding to sounds; no babbling or vocal turn-taking.
Not tracking with eyes; no smiling or social engagement.
Fever >100.4°F (38°C) at this age — call pediatrician.
Excessive sleepiness or inconsolable crying lasting hours.
Allergic reaction after new food: hives, swelling, vomiting, breathing trouble — emergency.
